title: Chapter 4 Quiz 1
description: Storing many values of the same type, and finding each by its position.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: What is an **array**?
options: A linear structure that stores values of the same type in memory, each found by an index
questions.explanation: An array groups data of the same type in reserved areas of RAM.

questions.question: What is the **index** of an array?
options: A pointer that gives the position of a cell
questions.explanation: The index locates each cell of the array.

questions.question: All the elements of an array have the same type.
questions.explanation: That is the difference with a record, whose fields can have different types.

questions.question: An index can be a constant or a variable of integer type.
questions.explanation: Either one can be used to select a cell.

questions.question: What does an array declaration need?
options: The type of the stored data
questions.explanation: Name, minimum index, maximum index and data type.

questions.question: Which declaration creates an array of 10 averages (real numbers) numbered 1 to 10?
questions.explanation: The syntax gives the index range between brackets, then ARRAY OF and the type.

questions.question: How many cells does an array [1..10] have?
How many cells does an array [0..9] have?
How many cells does an array [5..12] have?
Array T has the values 12, 7, 30, 4 in cells 1 to 4. Give the value of each expression.
questions.explanation: T[i] is the value in cell i.

questions.question: Arrays are stored in {{1}}, the volatile memory of the computer.
questions.explanation: Arrays live in RAM, so their content is lost when the program ends.
